purpose: Introduce a first-class bounded incident-repair lifecycle and reconcile construction lifecycle ownership so governance-only and already-merged defect repairs do not impersonate forward product selection or require routine meta-governance mutation.

lineage.outcome: Post-merge or governance defects can be repaired under one exact incident-bound authority without inventing a product node, reopening completed work, or allowing new product construction to masquerade as repair.
lineage.capability: Bounded incident-repair lifecycle and lifecycle-owner reconciliation

why_now: PR #211 repaired the trusted Steward bootstrap and was post-merge verified, but first use exposed two governance mismatches: already-merged/governance repairs cannot always bind a dependency-ready product node (#247), and ordinary governance incorrectly requires the immutable automation registry to mirror current construction lifecycle (#248). Qualification also exposed closure/event-stream and test-isolation obligations that belong to the same governance repair because they are necessary for the new lifecycle to terminate truthfully and remain portable across the required platform matrix.

implementation_contract.exclusive_mode: ACTIVE authority is either normal completion-graph construction or INCIDENT-REPAIR, never both.
implementation_contract.governance_repair: A GOVERNANCE incident repair must enumerate every authorized changed file in allowed_exact_paths, use no allowed_prefixes, keep product_code_allowed=false, and every enumerated changed file must remain inside governance/**, tests/governance/**, or the exact trusted Steward workflow path.
implementation_contract.merged_product_repair: MERGED_PRODUCT repair requires an exact target merge that predates the incident discovery main, and construction-sensitive repaired paths must already exist at that target merge.
implementation_contract.incident_truth: An ACTIVE incident repair names currently open repairable durable incidents through incident_repair_ids. incidents.jsonl is append-only event history and current incident truth is the latest row for each durable incident ID. An INACTIVE receipt carries no incident_repair_ids; exact terminal lineage is inert closure evidence through closed_incident_repair_ids plus closed_repair_receipt_id. Closure requires a latest durable RESOLVED event with resolved_at, a non-empty resolution_condition, non-empty evidence, exact binding to the ACTIVE repair receipt being closed, and exact binding to the new terminal closure receipt.
implementation_contract.runtime_truth: governance/current_state.json owns construction lifecycle. automation_registry.json remains declarative actor/authority bounds and is not a live runtime-state source. Runtime handoff derives current open incidents from the latest event per incident ID.
implementation_contract.trust: Lifecycle enforcement surfaces are protected behind explicit meta-governance reopen, including ordinary governance, incident-repair authority, context lifecycle, supervision, runtime handoff, Steward integration checking and staged consumer smoke. The pull_request_target workflow uses the trusted base copy; this bootstrap PR therefore also requires substantive manual review of the newly introduced helper before it can become base-owned for later PRs.

completion_proof: normal ACTIVE construction remains graph-node/dependency bound and is not retyped as incident repair by the specialized helper
GOVERNANCE repair passes with zero ACTIVE graph nodes and unchanged declarative automation lifecycle projection
GOVERNANCE repair rejects broad allowed path prefixes and admits only an exact changed-file manifest
MERGED_PRODUCT repair requires a pre-incident target merge and pre-existing repaired product paths
INACTIVE receipts cannot carry active incident_repair_ids; terminal closure preserves only inert closed_incident_repair_ids and closed_repair_receipt_id bound to the exact prior ACTIVE repair
append-only incident history permits repeated incident IDs while other durable JSONL registries retain unique IDs
current open-incident projections use the latest event per incident ID so a later RESOLVED event supersedes historical OPEN state without deleting history

a naked RESOLVED label cannot close a repair: the resolution event must carry evidence, resolution condition, resolved_at, exact ACTIVE repair receipt binding, and exact terminal closure receipt binding
new product files cannot be introduced through MERGED_PRODUCT repair mode
protected lifecycle enforcement surfaces cannot be changed by an ordinary PR without explicit meta-governance reopen
automation registry cannot reclaim runtime lifecycle ownership
governance-test Git maintenance suppression is scoped to governance tests and does not alter product/runtime Git policy
exact-head governance, full regression and staged consumer smoke pass on Linux, Windows and macOS
substantive exact-head review is terminal before merge
next_selection_rule: After this governance repair is merged and post-merge verified, close this exact ACTIVE repair receipt through inert evidence-bound closure lineage before selecting another #206 repair or unrelated product work. Keep #206 active until its full repair/verification contract is actually satisfied.
